rationale: This benchmark is a tiny (800 bytes of text, 4 functions) interpreter-style workload whose hot path is the eval dispatch loop, so the strategy is to concentrate control-flow obfuscation there while keeping per-iteration overhead low. FLA gets the highest security weight because flattening a dispatch loop destroys the switch/branch structure an analyst relies on most, but its RuntimeCost and SizeCost weights are held low-to-moderate since the loop executes continuously and code is tiny. IBR complements FLA by obscuring branch targets in that same loop at moderate cost. SUB and SPLIT are nearly free at runtime and very safe, so they get high cost-tolerance weights and apply broadly across the arithmetic-heavy evaluation code. BCF is the most expensive pass per iteration in a hot loop, so its RuntimeCost weight is kept low to restrict it to functions where security features strongly favor it. ICALL is limited (indirect-call conversion costs register pressure and speed in a tight loop, and this program has few call sites) and IGV is kept moderate since globals are minor here. All passes remain enabled with CorrectnessRisk tolerances at or above 0.5 so no pass is effectively disabled, preserving semantic fidelity of the evaluated expressions.
